lines.line: Summary: In Left 4 Dead 2 versus only the team playing the survivors earns points, and most of them come from how far each survivor gets along the chapter. The farthest point a survivor reaches is the one that counts, so a survivor who backtracks and dies keeps the distance made.

quoted: Points are only awarded to teams playing as the Survivors.
The distance traveled by each Survivor is the primary source of points for the Survivors.
The farthest distance a Survivor reaches is the score that Survivor gets (i.e., if a Survivor backtracks and dies, they will receive points for how far they traveled before backtracking).

lines.line: Tips: A survivor who is alive when the chapter ends is worth 25 more points to the team, unless they die in the safe room before its door shuts. Health and carried items no longer change the score, and reviving a dead survivor with a defibrillator costs 25 points.

quoted: Every Survivor that lives at the end of the chapter gets a 25-point bonus for their team.
If the Survivor makes it into the safe room and dies before the saferoom door closes, the 25-point bonus will not count.
The health or items of the Survivors no longer affects the score.
Reviving dead Survivors using a Defibrillator results in a 25-point penalty.

lines.line: Tips: If both teams reach the safe room with nobody dead, the team that did more damage as infected gets a 25-point tiebreak; equal scores with a death get no tiebreak. Both sides are told each time the survivors pass another quarter of the route.

quoted: In the event that both teams reach the safe room with no deaths, a 25-point tiebreak bonus is given to the team who did the most damage as Infected.
If both teams earn the same score in a level, but not everyone makes it to the safe room (i.e. someone dies), this tiebreaker does not occur.
The Infected and Survivor sides are notified at 25% intervals of the distance the Survivors have traveled.

lines.line: Tips: On pace, the wiki tells survivors to concentrate on progressing rather than hunting down a Hunter, especially in versus, yet its Realism Versus page says a slow, careful pace can beat blazing ahead for team points.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Hunter / The Survivors
quoted: your focus should be on progressing, not finding and killing the Hunter. This is especially true in Versus
sometimes moving slowly and cautiously is much better than trying to blaze ahead and get team points for the team

sections.name: Versus special infected spawn order and mixes

lines.line: Summary: When a versus infected player's wait to respawn is over, the AI Director assigns which special infected they become.

quoted: The AI Director determines which Special Infected "class" each player will spawn as once their spawn timer runs out and they enter spawn mode.

lines.line: Tips: In Left 4 Dead 2 versus, the four infected players nearly always get four different specials. The Director seldom deals out four pinners (Smoker, Charger, Hunter, Jockey), which keeps the team from pinning all four survivors in one move; Boomer and Spitter support instead of pinning.

quoted: In Left 4 Dead 2, the Infected team will almost always consist of four different Special Infected.
The Director rarely chooses a combination of four "pinning" Special Infected.
"Pinning" Infected are the Smoker, Charger, Hunter and the Jockey
This is so the Infected team cannot simply pin all four players at once, ending the round.
The Spitter and the Boomer do not pin in their attacks; instead, they play a support role to the other Infected

lines.line: Tips: The Tank is a random extra, at most one per level apart from fixed spawns, and your chance of getting him rises with your score. After the sides swap, the other team usually starts with the same specials in the same places and order.

quoted: The Tank is a special spawn, randomly occurring, with a maximum of one instance per level
Control of the Tank is given to a player on the Infected team randomly, with the odds of selection increasing with the player's score.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Difficulty and Game Modes / Versus Mode
quoted: players on the infected team will usually spawn in the same locations and sequence at the enemy team did.
if the last round began with a jockey, a boomer, a smoker, and a spitter, the other team will start with the same special infected after the swap.

lines.line: Tips: With fewer than three infected players, bots fill the empty slots and the Director may spawn two of the same type, or all the bot specials at once. With four infected players the respawn wait can reach 30 seconds, about 20 on average.

quoted: in the case of less than three Infected players, two Special Infected of the same type may spawn
The Director can also spawn all of the AI Special Infected at the same time.
an update in Left 4 Dead 2 has added Special Infected bots in its Versus mode
When there are four Infected, players can wait up to 30 seconds to respawn, although the average is closer to 20 seconds.

lines.line: Summary: When the respawn timer ends, a versus infected player goes into spawn mode, with a blue tint on the screen, and picks where to appear. The survivors cannot see a ghost, and other infected see it as a blue outline.

quoted: the Infected player will enter spawn mode which is indicated by a blue tint on screen.
The player must choose where they want to spawn.
The Infected player cannot be seen by the Survivor team.
Other Infected see spawning players as a blue outline.

lines.line: Tips: A spot has to be open ground that is neither too close to nor too far from the survivors, out of their sight, and not a restricted place such as the starting safe room before the survivors leave it.

quoted: can spawn in any unblocked space, provided that they are not too close to the Survivors or too far from them, they are not in the Survivors' line of sight, and they are not in a restricted area
the starting safe room prior to the Survivors vacating it

lines.line: Tips: A ghost passes through doors, breakable objects and some barricades, and nobody can hurt it, but dropping into an instant-kill zone kills it and restarts the timer, as a real death would.

quoted: Unspawned "ghost" infected can move through destructible objects and physics objects, such as doors and certain barricades.
These unspawned Infected cannot be harmed by other players, either Infected or Survivor
they will be killed without spawning if they fall into instant-kill zones
Infected who "die" in ghost mode restart their spawn timer as though they had actually died

lines.line: Tips: If you fall far behind, a message offers to put you in spawn mode at the survivors' location. Survivors can deny a spot by keeping it in sight or close, and a sudden rush that brings a key spot into view can ruin an ambush before the ghost spawns.

quoted: When an Infected gets to far behind the Survivors, a message will appear giving the Infected the option of moving closer to the group.
By pressing this, you will be in the respawn mode at the Survivors' location.
getting a spot into you or your teammates' line of sight or close proximity, denies your opponents spawning in that location.
suddenly rush and get a vital location into a Survivor's line of sight before an Infected player at that location has time to react and spawn
ruining the entire ambush plan

sections.name: Using the Witch as the infected team

lines.line: Summary: Nobody can play the Witch in versus, but she works as a trap: one hit from her incapacitates a survivor, so the infected team steers or lures survivors toward her.

quoted: You cannot play as the Witch, Common Infected, or Uncommon Infected.
On all difficulties, getting hit by a Witch will deal 100 damage, resulting in instant incapacitation.
you can use her in your tactics

lines.line: Tips: Smokers can drag survivors to her and Jockeys can steer them toward her. A Spitter can spit near her, since survivors dodging the acid may brush against her or end up close enough to set her off.

quoted: Smokers can drag Survivors to the Witch.
Jockeys can steer Survivors towards the Witch.
Spitters can protect the Witch by spitting acid near her.
Survivors will usually attempt to get away from the acid puddles quickly, which may cause them to touch the Witch or get near the Witch

lines.line: Tips: A crouching Hunter or Boomer in front of her hides her from the survivors, and a Boomer killed near her startles her and sends her after whoever shot him. A non-Tank infected player can also claw her once, which makes her almost enraged.

quoted: Hunters and Boomers can crouch in front of the Witch, obscuring her from the Survivors' sight.
if a Boomer is killed while the Survivors are relatively close to the Witch, the explosion will startle her, sending her after the person who killed the Boomer.
In Versus, non-Tank infected players can claw the Witch once upon spotting a Survivor, upon which she becomes near enraged.

lines.line: Tips: A Hunter can wait just out of sight near her and pounce whoever goes up to kill her, just before that survivor fires. Pouncing someone she has already downed costs the Hunter nothing and the victim dies twice as fast. Infected see her with a white outline that turns red as she gets angrier.

quoted: Experienced Hunter players normally crouch just out of sight near the Witch, waiting until a player runs up to attack the Witch and pouncing them just before they get a chance to fire.
If you pounce a Survivor as a Hunter while the Witch has already incapacitated someone and is attacking, you will not be damaged, and the Survivor will die twice as fast.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Players / Infected / Controls of the Infected
quoted: Docile Witches will have a white outline.
Witches in the process of being startled will have an outline that slowly changes from white to red

sections.name: Answering combined special attacks in versus

lines.line: Summary: A versus infected team often opens with a Boomer's bile, then sends Hunters in and has a Smoker pull someone away, and it picks on the survivors the bile missed. Staying together, holding fire while blind and cutting a Smoker's grab short are the answers.

quoted: The best tactic for coordinating your attacks is to let the Boomer vomit on as many people as he can.
Then, have the Hunters pounce from their hiding spots and make the Smoker pull someone away.
If the Boomer vomits on one person, then pounce or constrict the other three who haven't got Boomer bile on them!

lines.line: Tips: Against the Boomer, do not bunch up, so the bile cannot hit all four of you. If he is close, shove him and back away before shooting, and shoot only when he is far from every survivor.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Boomer / The Survivors
quoted: Avoid being too bunched up with the other Survivors.
There's no sense in all four of you getting puked on at once.
If the Boomer is too close, it's a good idea to melee-shove them, which will push them back to some degree, then back away to a safe distance before shooting
Only if the Boomer is sufficiently far away from both yourself and all other Survivors should you shoot them.

lines.line: Tips: If you are covered in bile, hold your fire because friendly fire is the likely result; shove instead and get to a defensible corner. Teammates should stay close to the biled survivor, and a pipe bomb can draw the horde away.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Boomer / The Survivors
quoted: Hold your fire! Since you can't see, friendly fire is the most likely result. Shove instead
Immediately find the nearest defensible corner
Stay close to the stricken Survivor.
Throw a pipe bomb to distract the horde

lines.line: Tips: When you hear a Smoker, stay close so nobody is alone. If one grabs you, you get only a few seconds to shoot him and break free, and if he is out of sight a teammate can shove you loose or shoot the tongue.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Smoker / The Survivors
quoted: When you or one of your teammates hear a Smoker, stay close together and watch out for each other.
When a Smoker grabs you, you will have a few seconds to free yourself by shooting the Smoker.
simply shove the Survivor free or shoot the tongue

lines.line: Summary: A Charger that carries or knocks survivors off a high ledge can incapacitate or kill them. The wiki calls a charge deadly beside ledges and cliffs.

quoted: Your charge is deadly near ledges and cliffs.
Avoid situations where the Charger can knock other Survivors off a high ledge, as it will either kill or incapacitate them.
If there's an area where there's a long drop or lethal area with no boundaries (such as a cliff or the top of a building), you should attempt to charge someone off

lines.line: Tips: As the Charger, ambush instead of charging from far away, since survivors dodge a long run, and do not spawn too early because your grunts give you away. A charge can start from a high place without stopping, and a survivor knocked aside near a ledge may be left hanging, or fall to their death if knocked far enough.

quoted: Avoid charges from a long distance. The Survivors will react quickly enough to dodge you
Ambushes will maximize your chance at successfully charging an enemy.
Spawning too early may alert the Survivors to your presence prematurely due to the Charger's loud grunts
Chargers can begin their charge from a high place without stopping.
Survivors that are knocked aside might be incapacitated by hanging if they are close to a high ledge when they are hit.
if they are knocked far enough past the ledge, they may fall to their deaths.

lines.line: Tips: As a survivor, never jump to dodge a charge, because even a slight height difference can mean heavy fall damage or instant death. Step aside instead, since he cannot change direction once he charges, and keep bots away because they do not try to dodge. Shoving does nothing; only explosives stumble him.

quoted: never try to jump when a Charger is charging. Even a slight height difference can result in catastrophic fall damage or even instant death.
The Charger can be fought similar to bullfighting.
Once he charges, he will be unable to change directions and will run into a straight line until he travels far enough or smashes into something.
Bots do not make any attempt to dodge a Charger's charge, so keep them away from the Charger if one is present.
The Charger is completely immune to melee shoves, so don't try to shove him.
only explosives — other than the Grenade Launcher — will work in stumbling him.

sections.name: Surviving Hunters and Jockeys in versus

lines.line: Summary: In versus a Hunter's pounce or a Jockey's landing knocks back survivors standing near the victim, which can leave them hanging from a ledge, so spread out just enough that the knockback does not reach your teammates.

quoted: the Hunter's pounce will generate knockback to nearby Survivors if it manages to pin someone. Try to stay away from each other, just to the point where the Hunter won't knockback nearby Survivors if he grabs someone.
if a Jockey jumps on someone, nearby Survivors will be knocked back, similar to a Hunter pouncing a Survivor with others nearby. In some areas, this can cause Survivors to hang onto a ledge.

lines.line: Tips: Against the Hunter, keep a teammate close, listen for the growl of one crouched and ready to pounce and warn the others, and shove just as the pounce begins to stun him. Versus Hunters often claw instead of pouncing, so a team health bar that drops unusually fast suggests one is nearby.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Hunter / The Survivors
quoted: Always have at least one buddy close at hand.
Listen for the distinctive growl the Hunter makes when he is crouched and ready to pounce.
Once you hear the cues, remind the other Survivors of the Hunter's presence
shove just as the Hunter starts his pounce. This will knock him back with a stun
On higher difficulties, and in Versus, the Hunter will often use their claw attack instead of pouncing the Survivors.
If someone's health meter drops unusually fast, it is usually an indicator that a Hunter is attacking nearby.

lines.line: Tips: Against the Jockey, shove him off and shoot him while he is stunned, and keep moving so you are hard to jump on. If one rides you, steer the opposite way to slow him so a teammate can knock him off. Deal first with Jockeys near hazards such as fire.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Jockey / The Survivors
quoted: Use melee shove to knock Jockeys off. They will be stunned so you can shoot them.
Keep moving so you are a difficult target to pounce on.
Move in the opposite direction of where the Jockey is steering you. This will make you move extremely slowly, allowing teammates to come and knock the Jockey off.
prioritize Jockeys if there are any hazards nearby, such as fire

sections.name: Surviving Smokers and Spitters in versus

lines.line: Summary: In versus the Smoker deals damage while he drags his victim. A Spitter has little health, and a few shots from any weapon kill her.

quoted: The Smoker now deals damage when he is dragging the Survivor.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Spitter / The Survivors
quoted: A Spitter does not have a lot of health, so a few shots from any weapon can kill her instantly.

lines.line: Tips: Smokers tend to strike from behind or above, though some spawn in front of you. A grabbed teammate is freed by killing or shoving the Smoker or by breaking the tongue, which grows back after about 15 seconds.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Smoker / The Survivors
quoted: Smokers tend to attack from behind or above your location, but some will spawn in front of you
Survivors can be rescued by killing/shoving the Smoker, or by attacking and breaking the tongue.
The Smoker's tongue will slowly grow back after being cut off and can be used to attack again after around 15 seconds.

lines.line: Tips: Shoot a Spitter from range with a Hunting Rifle or Sniper Rifle. If you are caught in her spit, get out at once, and after she dies wait for her acid to fade rather than walking around it, because going around or jumping does not work.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Spitter / The Survivors
quoted: Using a Hunting Rifle or a Sniper Rifle should take care of her easily at long range.
If you are caught in the spit, get away from it as soon as possible.
When the Spitter dies, she will leave a small pool of acid around her corpse.
Wait for the acid to disappear before moving further down.
Never try to go around a Spitter's acid
Jumping does not work either.

lines.line: Tips: Expect a versus Spitter to spit in your path in a tight hallway, leaving you to wade through the acid or wait for it to fade, which gives her team time to respawn.

quoted: If you are for some reason unable to spit on the Survivors directly in a tight hallway on Versus, spit in their path.
They will have two choices: Go through the acid and take damage, or wait until it disappears. If they choose to wait, this will allow your teammates time to respawn.

lines.line: Summary: A versus Tank has 6000 health and is handed straight to an infected player when the survivors enter the area the Director chose for him, and he is aggressive from the start.

quoted: The Tank has 6000 health points. The Director will also spawn them on the map when the Survivors enter a designed area, and let an Infected player take control immediately
The Tank is immediately aggressive

lines.line: Tips: Fire beats explosives here: set him alight with a Molotov or gas can and he takes damage over time, dying in about 30 seconds from full health, though in versus burning no longer slows him down.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Tank / The Survivors
quoted: Set the Tank on fire by using either a molotov or a gas can.
great for limited big damage, but not as effective as fire
fire, which always does guaranteed damage over time to the Tank

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Tank / The Infected
quoted: A Tank at full health that has been set on fire will die in thirty seconds
this loss of speed from fire in Versus was removed by patches in both games in October 2010

lines.line: Tips: Keep clear of cars, dumpsters, fallen trees and furniture, because he punches them at survivors and a hit incapacitates at once. Keep your distance and do not let him corner you.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Tank / The Survivors
quoted: Keep clear of cars, fallen trees, furniture, and dumpsters if the Tank is nearby.
which means an immediate incapacitation if said object hits any one of them
Keep your distance from the Tank if at all possible.
Never let the Tank back you into a corner as you can't go anywhere, and most likely you will be taken down.

lines.line: Tips: If he is pounding a downed teammate, shoving or hitting him in the back can pull his attention, which shooting does not. A melee swing does 500 damage to him whatever the weapon, and explosives do around 750.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Tank / The Survivors
quoted: another Survivor can aggravate the Tank and possibly draw its attention from its target by shoving and hitting it in the back.
Shooting a Tank won't have the same effect
Melee weapons deal 500 damage per swing at the Tank, regardless of what type.
Explosives deal around 750 damage to the Tank.

lines.line: Summary: The wiki calls coordination the most important factor in a versus match: a lone Hunter is killed before he does real damage, and a lone Smoker's victim is freed without much effort.

quoted: This is by far the most important factor in a Left 4 Dead Versus match.
If a Hunter pounces on his own, he will just get killed before he can do any real damage.
If a Smoker tries to constrict a Survivor they will just get freed without any real effort

lines.line: Tips: Open with the Boomer's bile on as many survivors as possible, then let the Hunters pounce from hiding and the Smoker pull someone away. If the bile lands on one survivor, go after the other three.

quoted: The best tactic for coordinating your attacks is to let the Boomer vomit on as many people as he can.
Then, have the Hunters pounce from their hiding spots and make the Smoker pull someone away.
If the Boomer vomits on one person, then pounce or constrict the other three who haven't got Boomer bile on them!

lines.line: Tips: A Smoker can drag a victim through a horde to open a path that a Charger then uses to scare off rescuers. A Spitter should spit over someone just pinned, especially by a Charger or Hunter, and a Charger does well to strike just after bile lands, going for the survivors who are not covered.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Smoker / The Infected
quoted: Smokers can drag a Survivor through a horde, creating a passage. The same passage can be used by a Charger to scare off the Survivors who rush to help their ensnared ally.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Spitter / The Infected
quoted: follow an another attacker Special Infected and immediately spit over a survivor they've just pinned especially from the likes of a Charger or Hunter
Attacking when Boomer bile has just covered the Survivors is a useful tactic. Aim for the Survivors who aren't covered

lines.line: Tips: The Boomer should usually spawn ahead of the survivors and the Smoker behind them to pull someone back, with Hunters near either to use the chaos. A Tank, a Charger or the horde works as a meat shield for a Hunter.

quoted: In general, the Boomer should spawn ahead of the Survivors so he can properly ambush while the Smoker should spawn behind to pull someone back. Hunters should be near the Smoker or the Boomer

drawn_from.part_of_page: Special Infected / The Hunter / The Infected
quoted: Hunters work significantly better with a meat shield (the horde, Charger, Tank).

lines.line: Summary: Charger ambush spots for the infected team on the first three chapters of Dead Center, The Hotel, The Streets and The Mall. The wiki's general rule is to hit survivors in a narrow space, a straight line or a tight clump.

quoted: always attack Survivors that are in a narrow area, in a straight line, or otherwise tight clump.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dead Center
quoted: The Hotel
The Streets
The Mall

lines.line: Tips: The Hotel: a survivor near a window with no ledge railing can be charged to their death. The fire on the first floor, between the kitchen and the lobby, burns far harder than usual, so pinning someone there also punishes anyone who comes to revive them.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dead Center
quoted: If a Survivor is by a window that doesn't have a railing on the ledge, charge at them, and you should bring the Survivor to their death.
try to pin them in the fire.
The fire between the kitchen and the main lobby does significantly increased damage
Teammates that are reviving the incapacitated Survivor will take massive damage from the fire as well

lines.line: Tips: The Streets: carry a survivor far from the group. The stretch just before the gun store is long and straight, so the survivors have almost no room to dodge. When they climb the dumpster ladder, get up there and charge, which usually knocks all of them back.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dead Center
quoted: The best you can do is try to carry a Survivor far away from the group.
Before the gun store, there is a long straight path to charge the Survivors with little room of dodging.
While the Survivors climb a ladder on the dumpster, climb up and charge at them; this will usually knock all of them back.

lines.line: Tips: The Mall: carry survivors off the higher floors. At an escalator, wait for the whole team to be on it and charge through the line the moment the first survivor reaches the end; anyone thrown clear may take fall damage.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dead Center
quoted: Try to carry the Survivors off of the higher floors.
Wait for all of them to start going up/down, and as soon as the first Survivor reaches the end of the escalator, charge straight into the escalator and through all of them.
The teammates who are sent flying might receive fall damage.

lines.line: Summary: Charger ambush spots for the infected team on the first four chapters of Dark Carnival: The Highway, The Fairgrounds, The Coaster and The Barns.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dark Carnival
quoted: The Highway
The Fairgrounds
The Coaster
The Barns

lines.line: Tips: The Highway: in the motel, take a survivor from the upper walkway and drag them over the edge. Hit the straggler just before the group drops down the hill into the swamp and the victim is left stranded, and near the end of the level you can drive one back down that hill.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dark Carnival
quoted: In the motel, try to grab a Survivor that is on the upper walkway. Pull them off to delay and damage them.
Charging the last Survivor before they can jump down the hill into the swamp will cause your victim to be stranded and will eventually perish.
Charge a Survivor all the way back down the hill near the end of the level.

lines.line: Tips: The Fairgrounds: once the survivors have climbed the building past Kiddie Land, the ramp behind the ladder lets you drive them back toward it, costing them time or a teammate.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dark Carnival
quoted: When the Survivors climb to the top of the building after Kiddie Land, there is a ramp behind the ladder that makes it possible to charge them back into Kiddie Land; this either makes them lose a lot of time or a fellow Survivor.

lines.line: Tips: The Coaster: at the start of the Tunnel of Love, as the survivors leave the safe room and climb the stairs, come at them from the far side and slam them into the wall. You can also spawn inside the safe room and charge toward the tunnel, since everyone is watching the tunnel.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dark Carnival
quoted: At the start of the Tunnel of Love, when the Survivors open the safe room door and go up the stairs, charge from the opposite side of the stairs, slamming all of them into the wall
A good variation on this is to spawn in the safe room, charge from the opposite direction towards the tunnel, because everyone is expecting a charge from the tunnel.

lines.line: Tips: The Barns: the rooftops are a good place to charge survivors off. In the long alleyway after the Crescendo Event they tend to line up, and hiding among the common infected helps.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Dark Carnival
quoted: The rooftops are a great place to charge Survivors off of.
survivors will often line up and allow you to bowl through them. Hiding in the swarms of Common Infected can make this easier

lines.line: Summary: Charger ambush spots for the infected team on the first three chapters of Swamp Fever: Plank Country, The Swamp and Shanty Town.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Swamp Fever
quoted: The Plank Country
The Swamp
Shanty Town

lines.line: Tips: Plank Country: when the survivors stand on the dock before the Crescendo Event, grab or knock one into deep water, which kills the one you grabbed and any you hit. The same works as they leave the ferry on the far side, from behind a tree. On the walkways, knocking them into the swamp slows them down.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Swamp Fever
quoted: When the Survivors are on the dock right before the Crescendo Event, try to grab, or better yet, knock one into the deep water. This will kill the Survivor you grabbed and the ones you hit instantly.
as soon as they exit the ferry at the other side of the map. Hide behind one of the trees then attempt to ambush and charge one of the survivors off the dock.
while the Survivors are on the walkways, try to get them to fall down into the swamp. This will slow them down considerably.

lines.line: Tips: The Swamp: taking survivors into the water helps, because the water slows their team down.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Swamp Fever
quoted: Taking the Survivors into the water is useful because their team will be slowed down by the water.

lines.line: Tips: Shanty Town: the water slows the survivors but not you, so use it to charge lone survivors. A few tight spots let you rush in and use the melee attack.

drawn_from.part_of_page: Good Ambush Spots / Left 4 Dead 2 / Swamp Fever
quoted: The water will slow down Survivors, but not you. Use this to charge lone Survivors.
There are a few tight points that you can rush in and use your melee attack.

lines.line: Summary: Survival sends wave after wave of infected at the team until everyone is dead or down. You cannot win it; the goal is to hold out for as long as you can and beat the record.

quoted: This game mode throws waves and waves of the Infected at the Survivors until they get fully overwhelmed via every survivor dying or getting incapacitated.
There is no way to win, as instead the goal is to survive as long as you can and set new records.

lines.line: Tips: Prepare before you set off the horde: gather as many supplies as you can and pick the best spot. Put special ammo and gas cans or propane tanks somewhere safe so the team can grab them fast if a Tank comes and no Molotov is left.

quoted: It is always best to hole up by gathering as much resources and finding the best spot possible before setting off the Horde.
preparing special ammo boxes and placing Gas Cans/Propane Tanks in a secure spot can allow the team to grab it quickly in the event of a Tank attack if they do not have any Molotovs on hand
Place everything you need in the place you plan to hold out in, so you do not have to leave your area for supplies and risk getting attacked easily.

lines.line: Tips: Judge a spot by its entrances, the ammo and supplies near it, escape routes, high ground and how far you can see. Keep the entrances to one or two with two survivors covering each, which matters most against a Tank unless you have an escape plan.

Try to keep the number of entry points down to two or one, if possible, so that at least two survivors are covering each entrance.
This is the most important consideration for when you have to fight Tanks, unless you have an escape plan when the Tank comes.

lines.line: Tips: The wiki lists set times for Tanks, the first at 0:40 and two Tanks together at 5:30 and 11:30. New hordes pause around 3:50 to 4:25, 9:00 to 9:35 and 12:00 to 12:30, when only special infected can spawn, which makes those gaps good for healing or ammo runs.

quoted: Tanks and hordes spawn at consistent times during the first 12 minutes.
Tanks will consistently spawn at 0:40,
Take note of the double Tank spawns at 5:30 and 11:30

New hordes of common infected do not spawn from approximately 3:50-4:25, 9:00-9:35, and 12:00-12:30; this means that, during those times, the only infected that can spawn are Special Infected, making those times ideal for ammo runs, healing, or other actions that would be risky otherwise.

lines.line: Summary: Realism Versus plays like versus with the same scoring, but the survivors follow Realism rules: tougher common infected, no glows around survivors or items, and a Witch that kills in one hit.

quoted: Realism Versus follows normal rules for Versus in terms of gameplay style and scoring, but makes things harder for the Survivors as they are bound by Realism rules.
Common Infected are tougher, there are no glows around Survivors or items, and the Witch can kill in one hit

lines.line: Tips: As a survivor, never run off, because teammates cannot see you through walls. Listen for a Hunter's growl or a Smoker's cough and call it out, and use a microphone, since typing leaves you open to attack. Do not dash for special-tier weapons if the infected may be camping them.

quoted: Never run off. Ever.
since visibility through walls is removed, teammates will probably never make it to the ailing player in time.
Listen carefully for the growl of a Hunter, or the cough of a Smoker.
It's highly recommended to use a microphone to communicate with the teammates as typing with a keyboard always renders the Survivor vulnerable to any Infected attack.
Don't rush off for the Special Tier weapons like the Grenade Launcher or M60 if you can help it
if the Special Infected get smart, they'll camp those spots and wait for players to run into the ambush.
Players are unable to see their fellow Survivors through walls

lines.line: Tips: As the infected, lone survivors are easy prey, and Tier 2 weapon spots and visible healing supplies are worth camping because survivors rush to them. Infected damage is higher, so even a short Charger life can cripple a team, and a Jockey can down anyone whatever their health because the others must first find the victim.

quoted: Lone Survivors are always easy fodder.
Try to camp Tier 2 weapon locations or spots with clearly visible healing supplies, as the chances of Survivors rushing to those spots are extremely high.
Infected damage is increased here so even if a player only gets in a couple of hits as a Charger, the attack could cripple their team greatly.
in Realism Versus, a Jockey can easily incapacitate a Survivor regardless of health, since the other players first need to find the victim to shove the Jockey off.

lines.line: Tips: Infected still see survivor auras normally, but the Tank does not see the red glow around cars and other objects he can punch. A later patch took out every defibrillator and every first aid kit except the ones the survivors start each map with.

quoted: Players on the Infected team will still see auras normally, except that the Tank will not see red auras around cars and other objects that he can punch at the Survivors.
A later patch removed all Defibrillators from Realism Versus, as well as all First aid kits other than the ones that the Survivors begin each map with.
